acceptance_criteria: AC-1 One documented command brings up PostgreSQL, runs the existing Flyway migrations V1 to V7, starts the service and serves the frontend.
AC-2 A browser on the documented localhost address reaches the running shell, and its default screen is the empty state because the database is empty.
AC-3 The database starts empty on a fresh volume, and the document names the exact command that resets it to empty.
AC-4 No credential value is committed: the compose setup reads secrets from the environment or a git-ignored file, and the document says which.
AC-5 The service is not exposed beyond the local machine by default, and the document states the bound interface.
AC-6 The existing integration suite still passes unchanged.
AC-7 The startup is actually executed in the foreground and its real output, including any failure, is reported in SESSION_CLOSE.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_12.md (FROZEN) section 4: the required first state is a clean, empty database with the UI and its menus visible and nothing pre-populated. project/QUEUE.md row ui2_b1_12_deployment_slice carries the container work.
baseline.sequencing: Runs alongside the M3 screen work; it packages what exists rather than changing it.

invariants: A clean, empty database is the required first state; nothing is seeded.
No credential, management address, device name or serial enters a tracked file.
No vendor data collection and no device contact: the standing collection gate holds.
No HTTP surface gains a write capability in this movement.
New feature code is Java written from scratch; the repository's Python scripts are know-how only.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Produce the deployment slice that stands the whole UI 2.0 product up on one machine with one command: PostgreSQL, Flyway migrations, the Spring Boot service and the built frontend, reachable in a browser on localhost, with a documented way to stop it and reset the database.
output_contract: A working local deployment slice and its operator document
SESSION_CLOSE with exact changed files, the real startup output, the reset command, and any step that could not be executed in this environment stated plainly as not executed

recommended_reasoning.reason: Packaging work over an existing, already-booting stack; the risk is credential handling and an unverified startup claim, not algorithmic difficulty.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law
Reuse the existing migrations and configuration rather than introducing a second source of truth
Bind to the local machine only; do not publish a port on all interfaces
Do not open a pull request and do not merge; commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE
Run the validation plan in the foreground and wait for real results before SESSION_CLOSE
risks: Committing a credential into a compose file or environment file
Seeding the database and breaking the required empty first state
Publishing the service on a non-local interface
Claiming a successful startup that was never executed

in: A compose file and its container definitions under ui2/
Service configuration needed to serve the built frontend and connect to the containerised database
One short operator document: start, stop, reset, and where the app appears
out: Any change to frontend components or screens
Any schema or migration change beyond what already exists
Any vendor data collection or device contact
Any credential value committed to the repository
Any production or server deployment; this is a local run

validation_plan: frontend build: npm --prefix ui2/frontend run build
stack startup executed in the foreground, then the documented reset command
